3. Added an "Immunity" system, some enemies are immune to certain types of elements

4. Added a hidden item system that will be displayed if you have an item compass equipped

5. Added new weapons

6. Added new skills

8. Added a sprite of Laisa using a staff

9. Added breakable items in Dreadfort

10. Added breakable item "Void Metal"

11. Added a new tutorial "Hidden Item"

13. Added a special mechanic for an enemy

14. Added new attacks

7. Fixed Esteem rising above max on certain items Occasions

9. Fixed bug where Laisa's head was "cut off" by the vendors in Largefield

10. Fixed current map not appearing correctly in save

11. Fixed sound options not working in main menu

12. Fixed Lava not appearing in Strongarm cave

13. Fixed enemies sometimes attacking after dying

14. Fixed "Always Run" not working properly

15. Fixed volume options in in-game options

16. Fixed certain sidequests being able to be abused to get infinite items

17. Fixed sidequests not deleting items correctly from inventory

notes.title: Esteem game release on 24indie.com
notes.notes:
A Visual Hug for Your Soul

All in all, you can see it isn’t just another pixelated indie game. Esteem – The Little Wolf Saga is a handcrafted, lovingly drawn world. Every map, character, and even item oozes originality. In fact, each location tells a story, and every character pulses with a personal vibe. Because they’re actually based on real people!
The art is colorful but not overwhelming, delicate without being fragile. In summary, a perfect metaphor for the game’s emotional core. Given these points, big credit again to Laisa, Michels, and Empty for character designs. The characters aren’t just visual candy but soul food.
